title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: The page image is upside down. It is not a Grothendieck manuscript page. It is page 163 of a typescript in English that was evidently reused as scrap paper; Grothendieck's handwritten 'motifs sur F_p' notes on the neighbouring pages are presumably on the other side or on other sheets. The content (two-dimensional normal local rings, rational singularities, the group H, configuration diagrams from §24, Theorem 25.1 (ii), Remarks 25.2/25.3) matches Joseph Lipman's 'Rational singularities, with applications to algebraic surfaces and unique factorization' (Publ. Math. IHES 36, 1969). It is most likely a pre-publication typescript circulated at IHES around 1968. In that paper H is the divisor class group of R, which is finite for rational singularities. §25 treats factorial (H trivial) rational singularities. Theorem 25.1 (ii) is the E8 case z^2 + x^3 + y^5 = 0, characterising rational singularities with trivial H and diagram (k). Remark 25.3 extends this to residue fields R/m that need not be algebraically closed, assuming char ≠ 2. The other rational singularities with trivial H have their configuration diagrams listed with defining equations. The first entry, diagram '1-3', is z^2 + ax^3 + bx^2y + cxy^2 + dy^3 = 0, where the reduced binary cubic form is irreducible over R/m. Geometrically, this is a D4-type double point: after a residue-field extension, the three outer components of the D4 graph become Galois-conjugate. Over R/m this gives one central curve attached to an irreducible curve of degree 3 over the residue field; with trivial H this is a non-split D4. This is a Galois-twisted (non-split) form of a factorial rational double point. Proofs are stated to be computational and omitted.
errors: Typographical error in the typescript: 'we have actually show' should read 'shown'. The mathematics is consistent with Lipman's published Remark 25.3.

ideas.what: Classification of factorial (trivial class group H) rational surface singularities over arbitrary residue fields of char ≠ 2, by configuration diagram and explicit equations; e.g. the twisted D4 form z^2 + (irreducible binary cubic) = 0
ideas.modern_name: Factorial rational double points / non-split forms of ADE singularities (Lipman's classification)
ideas.where_published: Lipman, 'Rational singularities...', Publ. Math. IHES 36 (1969), §25, Remark 25.3

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of Lipman's published IHES paper on rational singularities, reused as scrap paper in the Grothendieck motives folder. It contains no Grothendieck mathematics, and its content is published and credited to Lipman. Its only interest is archival: the sheet suggests Lipman's typescript was circulating at IHES around 1968, which helps date the paper of the motives notes.
transcription_corrections: The page is physically upside down in the scan.
It is an English typescript (page 163), apparently of Lipman's 'Rational singularities...', not Grothendieck's handwriting.
'we have actually show' is the original typo, not a transcription error.
In the cubic form the bars denote residues: ā x^3 + b̄ x^2 y + c̄ x y^2 + d̄ y^3.
